//: McLeod Country Golf Club, Mt Ommaney. OSM carries all 18 golf=hole centrelines with refs 1-18 (plus a golf=tee node at each line start and a golf=pin node at each line end -- the way endpoints, so tee=first point, green=last point for every hole). It carries NO greens, fairways, bunkers or water, so the greens are ovals at the mapped pin and the fairways/bunkers are traced from open Esri aerial imagery (the sparse-OSM path in the add-play-course skill).
//par: Par comes from the published card (out 37 / in 34 = 71) and is corroborated hole-for-hole by the OSM lengths: every hole falls in its par's length class.
//si: Stroke index and Slope come from a club card photographed on the course (a Cardiac Challenge 4-Person Ambrose, White tee, S/R 67.0 Slope 124). That card is an EVENT LAYOUT, not the standard course: it plays 1-6, 7A, 7, 8 | 9-15, 17, 18 -- a short 7A inserted, 16 dropped -- for par 68 over 5068 m, and holes 7/11/12/14 are played off temporary short tees. So only the layout-independent parts are used. The SIs of the 17 standard holes on that card are exactly 1-17, with 7A taking 18, which means the club SIs were kept and hole 16 (the shortest hole) holds SI 18 -- that is the allocation baked here, and it forms a clean 1-18 permutation. Slope 124 is taken as the White-tee figure. CR is deliberately NOT taken: 67.0 rates the 5068 m par-68 event layout, and applying it to the par-71 standard course would make (cr - par) = -4 and understate every course handicap by about 3 strokes. Without cr the app falls back to CR = par, which is neutral and safe. Replace it when the club standard card turns up.
//tees: tees.white = the card distance in metres (yards/1.0936). 14 of 18 holes agree with the OSM line to within 3%. The four that don't (1, 12, 13, 16) have cardPlaceWhite so the tee sits at the card distance back along the play line -- OSM mapped a different tee on those (hole 12 has two printed tees, 12W and 12M, on the club course map). No cr/slope: the club's ratings could not be verified, and the app falls back to neutral (113 / CR = par) for net scoring.
name: McLeod Country Golf Club

course.src: OSM routing + aerial bunkers + club course map

//bunkers: Bunkers are traced from a georeferenced Esri aerial (scripts/play/fetch-aerial.mjs -> from-aerial-hazards.mjs), NOT from the course map -- the map places them corridor-relative, which the aerial showed is not close enough for a hazard. Detection favours precision over recall: sand must be bright, compact, surrounded by turf and markedly brighter than that turf, which is what separates it from bare dirt and cart paths. So the 41 that survive are real and absolutely positioned, but grass-faced and tree-shaded bunkers do not show. Water/trees/rough/fairways stay from the course map; water is deliberately never taken from imagery (dark shadow and dark water are the same in RGB).
//geom: This config builds the ROUTING geometry only (surveyed greens as ovals + ribbon fairways). Bunkers, water, trees, rough and the real drawn fairway corridors are then traced from the club course map by scripts/play/from-course-map.mjs (see mcleod-country-golf-club.coursemap.json), which overwrites the fairways and keeps these greens. Re-run gap-fill FIRST, then from-course-map, or the traced hazards are lost. On a machine that can reach services.arcgisonline.com, setting fairwayRibbonM to 0 with traceFairways/traceBunkers true would instead source corridors and sand from aerial imagery.
